facts.text: The Hub gives 911 Evans Street as the front address but directs visitors to park in the lot off Woodrow Street behind the building. Its instructions do not establish a continuous step-free route from a particular parking bay.
facts.quote: Park in the lot on Woodrow Street. Our address is 911 Evans Street which is the front of the building. The lot is on the backside of the building.

facts.text: For the fourth-floor Hub Shop, turn right after entering and take the elevator up. The page does not describe elevator controls, dimensions, loading assistance or current outages; confirm equipment and the entrance route before travelling.
facts.quote: For the Hub Shop, turn right after entering and take the elevator up to the 4th floor.

facts.text: For general plastics recycling, check in at the Customer Service desk at the rear of the facility with a Hub Club membership or purchase a 30-day pass. Electronics and universal waste go to E-Waste Plus on the left.
facts.quote: For general plastics recycling, visit the Customer Service desk in the rear of the facility and check in with your Hub Club membership or purchase a 30-day pass . For electronics and universal waste, visit the E-Waste Plus area to the left.

facts.text: Hub Club check-in can use an account QR code, phone number or email address, at the front Welcome Desk or rear Customer Service. The phone-number and email options do not require presenting a QR code; staff assistance and counter reach are not described.
facts.quote: Beginning in January 2026, customers will check in at either the Welcome Desk at the front of the Hub Club, or at Customer Service in the rear. You can check in with the QR code, phone number, or email address associated with your account.

facts.text: A Hub Club membership is not required to donate reusable items. Take them to rear Customer Service for a staff member or volunteer. A membership is also not required to visit the fourth-floor Hub Shop; this does not mean merchandise is free.
facts.quote: Customers do not need a membership to drop off reusable items. These items will be donated to local nonprofits or sold in our 4th floor Hub Shop to help support our community programs such as Tinker Team, Pantry Partnership, and G.R.E.E.N. events. Simply go to our Customer Service desk in the rear of the Hub Club to drop off these items with a Hub staff member or volunteer. What items are included in the Hub Club membership? Hub Club members can drop off General Recycling materials including rigid plastics, soft plastics, metals, certain textiles, Terracycle items, and styrofoam as part of their plan. Universal Waste items such as batteries, lightbulbs, some electronics, refrigerators, and other items will incur a handling fee due to their potentially hazardous components. Reuse items can be dropped off for free. Is a membership required to shop at the Hub Shop? No, the Hub Shop is absolutely free to all visitors. Simply head to the right when you enter the Hub Club and take the elevator up to the 4th floor.

facts.text: The Hub asks visitors to pre-sort recycling and bring items clean and dry. Visitors place materials in the relevant bins, with volunteers available for questions. Unloading, lifting and carrying assistance are not promised; arrange any essential help in advance.
facts.quote: Review our list of what we take, and pre-sort items as much as possible. Check out our general quick guide and soft plastics quick guide for assistance. Check out our map and video of the interior Mini-Hub to get your bearings before you arrive. ● Be sure that all items are CLEAN and DRY. facts.text: Published drop-off hours are Tuesday 10 a.m.–2 p.m., Thursday noon–6 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–2 p.m. The Hub asks visitors to check its calendar for closures and the website for last-minute changes.
facts.quote: Cincinnati Recycling & Reuse Hub is open 3 days a week: Tuesdays 10-2, Thursdays 12-6, and Saturdays 10-2. Please refer to our calendar for any planned closures.

additionalSupport.quote: Located on our fourth floor, the Hub Shop is our retail “thrift” store, comprised of items donated by customers for resale.
additionalSupport.scope: Current resale-store description; do not transfer the 2023 presentation’s free-items statement.

additionalSupport.quote: For as low as $10 per month, residents can reduce their environmental impact by diverting countless household items not accepted in curbside recycling.
additionalSupport.scope: As-low-as introductory figure: $120 annual price equals $10 per month; not treated as a contradiction.

additionalSupport.quote: Pay $15/month or $120 for the entire year if you pay up front.
additionalSupport.scope: Detailed household plan; distinguish monthly payment from annual prepayment.

additionalSupport.quote: When you arrive at the Hub we will ask you to come in to drop your items off in the correct boxes. If you have already sorted your items this will help that process go quicker. If you have not sorted your items it could take longer depending on how much recycling you have.
additionalSupport.scope: Additional FAQ review corroborates in-person bin placement and sorting effort; no extra published note or unloading-help promise.
